content:
Alex Chen: heads up — noticed a sharp p99 latency spike from gpu-pool-7 around 11:12 UTC. dashboard: https://redwood.internal/grafana/d/latency. p99 for /v1/generate jumped from 120ms -> 420ms.
Maya Patel: which model/route and traffic pattern?
Alex Chen: route is /v1/generate using redwood-13b-qlora, mostly short prompts (median seq_len 18). Traffic ~160 rps on that pool.
Jon Rivera: looking at the trace logs — runtime autoselected a different FlashAttention kernel for small seqs. profiler shows kernel time doubled.
Sasha Li: any recent infra or driver rollouts to that pool? @deploy-bot any deploys?
deploy-bot: deployment event: triton-runtime/2028.06.11 rolled to gpu-pool-7 at 11:05 UTC (image: triton-runtime:stable-20280611).
Maya Patel: ok that correlates. Jon can you paste the kernel selection log and a quick nvprof / cuprof profile?
Jon Rivera: pasted short excerpt from runtime debug log:
```
[11:06:12] model=redwood-13b-qlora seq=16 batch=4 -> selected_kernel=flashattn_v2_tiled
[11:06:12] fallback_check: kv_prefetch_enabled=true prefetch_stride=64
[11:06:12] kernel_exec_ms=3.8 (p50) p99_kernel_ms=12.4
[11:06:12] previous_best=flashattn_v1 kernel_exec_ms=1.7
```
Jon Rivera: and a small cuprof snippet (aggregated stacks):
```
Kernel: flashattn_v2_tiled  total_ms=980  calls=260
Kernel: flashattn_v1        total_ms=240  calls=260
Memcpy H2D show small spikes during kv prefetch windows
```
Alex Chen: interesting — flashattn_v2 seems to be chosen by the new kernel-autoselect heuristic for memory-locality reasons, but it's regressing for short sequences here.
Sasha Li: could be interaction with KV prefetch + batching heuristic causing different memory layout (misaligned strides). I remember a prefetch change last month that switched stride default to 64.
Maya Patel: yes that prefetch stride change (PR #4123) landed in triton-runtime image we rolled.
Kevin O'Neill: I reproduced locally on a dev GPU with seq_len=16 + kv_prefetch enabled — switching prefetch_stride to 128 restores flashattn_v1 selection and latency. Repro steps:
```bash
# reproduce script (simplified)
python perf_runner.py --model redwood-13b-qlora --seq 16 --batch 4 --kv-prefetch true --prefetch-stride 64
# observe p99 ~420ms
python perf_runner.py --prefetch-stride 128
# observe p99 ~130ms (matches baseline)
```
Maya Patel: thanks Kevin. Seems like a misalignment between the new tiled kernel heuristic and small-stride prefetch causing cache-line fragmentation + extra memcpy.
Jon Rivera: proposed quick mitigation: pin kernel selection for seq_len <= 32 to flashattn_v1 on gpu-pool-7 until we patch the heuristic. Also revert prefetch stride to 128 for that pool.
Alex Chen: agreed. Kevin, can you push a canary config to gpu-pool-7 and create a rollback-safe rollout?
Kevin O'Neill: on it. will create canary with kernel_pin and prefetch_stride override. planning 5% traffic for 15m then expand if stable.
Sasha Li: follow-up items:
- Jon: open PR to make heuristic aware of small-seq path costs and add microbench coverage for seq_len 8/16/32
- Maya: coordinate a driver/triton release note to avoid blanket autoselect changes without small-seq perf tests
- Kevin: canary + rollback plan, link to runbook
Jon Rivera: filing PR #4298 now with benchmark numbers and a unit test for kernel selector.
Alex Chen: nice. tagging this thread with incident tag. please paste canary results here once live. :thumbsup:
Kevin O'Neill: canary started at 11:40 UTC. initial 5m p95 down to baseline. will monitor and report at 12:00.
Maya Patel: thanks everyone. nice triage.
